content:
Following yesterday's system update that included security patches, Apple has now published the security content details for Safari 26.6.1. Here are the relevant details.

Codex appears multiple times in the CVE acknowledgements list

Apple has today updated its "Apple Security Updates" page, publishing details of the bug fixes included in Safari 26.6.1, which is now available for macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia.

According to the document, this update contains 22 CVEs, all related to WebKit, two of which involve "processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to memory corruption."

Notably, as with recent security updates, OpenAI Codex Security appears nine times, further highlighting the increasingly important role of AI tools in finding security vulnerabilities in Apple software.

Below is Apple's full security content for Safari 26.6.1:

Safari 26.6.1 Released: August 18, 2026 WebKit Available for: macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected Safari crash Description: An out-of-bounds access issue was addressed by improved boundary checks. WebKit Bugzilla: 317632 CVE-2026-64784: Janggoon Lee (Out of Bounds), OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Description: The issue was addressed by improved memory handling. WebKit Bugzilla: 313452 CVE-2026-43795: wwwlk WebKit Bugzilla: 318348 CVE-2026-65338: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to memory corruption WebKit Bugzilla: 318405 CVE-2026-65341: Henock Habte WebKit Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed by improved locking. WebKit Bugzilla: 321480 CVE-2026-64782: Seonwook Kim, Shubham Chaskar, lattice, Josef Korbel WebKit Description: The issue was addressed by improved input validation. WebKit Bugzilla: 321484 CVE-2026-64781: Thomas Guillem WebKit Description: The issue was addressed by improved state management. WebKit Bugzilla: 321517 CVE-2026-65351: Niels Hofmans WebKit Bugzilla: 316996 CVE-2026-65340: Claudio Bozzato and Francesco Benvenuto (Cisco Talos), Josef Korbel (Citadelo) WebKit Bugzilla: 317142 CVE-2026-65337: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317349 CVE-2026-65336: Josef Korbel WebKit Bugzilla: 316723 CVE-2026-65335: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317603 CVE-2026-65333: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317450 CVE-2026-65332: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317611 CVE-2026-65331: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process crash Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed by improved memory management. WebKit Bugzilla: 316347 CVE-2026-64715: Hossein Lotfi (@hosselot) (TrendAI Zero Day Initiative) WebKit Description: The issue was addressed by improved checks. WebKit Bugzilla: 316918 CVE-2026-64780: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed by improved state management. WebKit Bugzilla: 316791 CVE-2026-65334: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed by improved memory handling. WebKit Bugzilla: 317317 CVE-2026-43794: Dung Do (@_piers2) (Calif.io) WebKit Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process termination WebKit Bugzilla: 313703 CVE-2026-64787: Sota Sugiyama, Shubham Chaskar WebKit History Impact: Visiting a maliciously crafted website may lead to sensitive data exposure WebKit Bugzilla: 315528 CVE-2026-64778: Mohit Negi WebKit Storage WebKit Bugzilla: 321485 CVE-2026-64779: Shubham Chaskar, Tommy DeVoss (Braze Security Team, @thedawgyg) Additional recognition WebKit We would like to acknowledge Henock Habte for their assistance.
